text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 — Multi-region failover started: autoswitch triggered from eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 due to reported AZ networking degradation in eu-west-1. Investigating cross-region routing and DNS behaviour. Pager duty alert: PD-4629.

pagerduty-bot: Paging mike (oncall) — please acknowledge. Incident priority: SEV-2. Escalation path: oncall -> infra -> eng-sre.

mike (oncall): acked. I’m on it. Quick summary of what I see: increased 5xx from eu-west-1 across public API ~11:02 UTC, traffic shift to us-east-1 started 11:06 UTC, some customer sessions still returning errors / timeouts.

alana (sre): I’m seeing a lot of 502/504 spikes from the edge in eu-west-1 even after weight update. Backend stats show healthy instance pools in us-east-1 but request volume isn’t matching expected post-failover. Could be DNS caching or LB sticky sessions. :eyes:

jay (infra): On the infra side, Route53 weights were updated by the failover playbook at 11:06. However BGP telemetry shows partial withdrawal of routes from eu-west-1 peering before weights flipped — looks like a routing flap at the cloud-provider level between AZs.

mike (oncall): Customer impact check: support channel shows ~7 customers reporting elevated errors, mostly EU traffic. Not seeing full outage, degraded for some apps with aggressive DNS caching. Natalie, can you surface any high-priority customer threads?

natalie (pdm): Confirmed — two customers on Dedicated reported client errors and session resets. Support sent interim message: "we're actively failing over; expect degraded latencies as traffic moves". They need an ETA for full recovery.

ops-bot: Runbook link: <https://confluence.redwood/workflows/multi-region-failover|multi-region failover runbook> — recommended checklist applied: weight-update -> health-checks -> route verification -> cache purge.

mike (oncall): Action list I'm starting now:
- validate Route53 weight changes
- check edge/cache invalidation and CDN DNS TTLs
- verify backend KV cache warmup in us-east-1
- open cloud-provider support ticket for inter-AZ routing flap

mike (oncall): Quick checks:
```
# verify DNS from multiple vantage points
dig +short api.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
dig +short api.redwood.com @1.1.1.1
# curl to edge from us-east and eu-west digests
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood.com/health
```

alana (sre): Logs: lots of errors in the reverse-proxy linking clients to old session shards. KV cache TTLs caused many requests to be routed to eu-west origin still. Shards in us-east are warm but some requests carried connection affinity.

jay (infra): Evidence from edge telemetry: the weight update succeeded but DNS resolvers (some large enterprise ISPs) still cached eu-west IPs with low TTL respect. Additionally, provider-level anycast announced eu-west prefixes intermittently which caused some traffic to keep going to eu-west and hit degraded AZ. That explains the mixed behavior.

mike (oncall): Immediate mitigations in flight:
- increase Route53 weight to 100% us-east for api.redwood.com (force traffic)
- set short TTL (30s) on the apex record temporarily
- purge edge caches for known customer prefixes (where possible)
- add temporary header to instruct clients to re-resolve via 307 redirect for new sessions (if app supports)

jay (infra): I’ve put in the Route53 change and TTL update. Cloud provider ticket opened: CR#88921 — we requested peering team to confirm no lingering anycast announcements.

ops-bot: Change recorded: route53 update by jay at 11:21 UTC.

mike (oncall): After forcing 100% weight -> us-east and TTL=30, we're seeing a reduction in errors from edge tests but still ~10–15% of EU-origin requests return 502s. Might be resolver cache on customer side or ISP.

alana (sre): We should consider a short-lived transparent proxy that rewrites Host header to us-east canonical IP for requests hitting eu-west front doors. That will avoid depending on client DNS. Manual but faster than waiting for caches.

jay (infra): Implementing HTTP-level rewrite at the edge (fastly/our CDN) now — will direct traffic to us-east origin without requiring client DNS changes. Rolling config in 2m.

mike (oncall): Monitoring: aggregate 5xx rate dropping from 6% -> 1.2% in last 10m. Latency still elevated for some customers. Support, please update affected customers with: "traffic fully shifted but propagating DNS caches may still cause intermittent errors for up to 5–10 minutes".

natalie (pdm): Messaging sent to impacted customers. They want RCA when done. Also asking about SLA credits window — flagging for billing.

ops-bot: Edge rewrite deployed by jay at 11:35 UTC.

alana (sre): Verify scripts:
```
# edge health from eu vantage
curl -H "Host: api.redwood.com" https://eu-edge-01.redwood.local/health -v
# backend session shard check
ssh jump@ops "redis-cli -h kv-eu-west get session:<id>"
```

mike (oncall): Good news — the rewrite cut the 502s for the fluxing sessions. 5xx back to baseline for most customers. Still keeping incident open while we validate cloud provider fix and propagate final cleanup.

jay (infra): Provider confirmed there was an AZ-level peering flap and some prefixes were intermittently announced from secondary peering points causing partial traffic to remain in eu-west. They claim peering is stable now, closing CR#88921 in 45m.

alana (sre): Tasks for recovery window:
- revert forced route53 weight and TTL to normal rollback policy
- remove temporary edge rewrite when DNS resolvers honor new records
- capture traffic-snapshot for postmortem (who still hit eu-west after failover)
- validate KV cache consistency and eviction logs

mike (oncall): Handoff plan: I need to go offline in ~25m. Alana, can you take rotation and own post-incident checks / RCA start?

alana (sre): I’ll take it. Summary for handoff:
- root cause: AZ-level networking degradation in eu-west-1 triggered automatic failover -> weight update to us-east.
- main complication: partial anycast/peering announcements + client DNS caching led to mixed traffic and sticky sessions hitting degraded eu-west nodes, producing 502/504.
- mitigations performed: Route53 force to us-east, TTL down to 30s, edge HTTP rewrite to redirect remaining eu-west traffic -> us-east, purge caches, cloud-provider ticket.
- outstanding: confirm provider closure, revert temp config, prepare postmortem with timeline and customer impact list.

mike (oncall): Notes for RCA: include per-customer hit list, timeline of route53 changes, BGP telemetry slices, and a small runbook improvement: add automatic temporary edge-rewrite step if DNS-based failover leaves >5% traffic in degraded region after 2min.

natalie (pdm): I’ll coordinate customer comms and gather exact SLA impact windows. Please tag me in the postmortem draft.

ops-bot: Handoff recorded: mike -> alana at 11:50 UTC. Incident status: active -> mitigated (awaiting cleanup & RCA).

alana (sre): Taking ownership. I’ll run the post-incident checklist and start a timeline doc. Will ping here when revert is scheduled. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

mike (oncall): Thanks all. I’m available on pager for any follow-ups before I go offline.

incident-bot: Incident SEV-2 mitigated, status: monitoring. If any regressions observed, reactivate or reopen PD-4629.

ops-bot: Links: cloud ticket CR#88921, runbook, support threads (internal).
